Ivan Turgenev, On the Eve, translated by Constance Garnett.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/ivan-turgenev/on-the-eve/constance-garnett

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Ivan Turgenev, the author, died 1883 (Wikidata Q42831). Citizenship: Russian Empire.
- Constance Garnett, the translator, died 1946 (Wikidata Q2495818). Citizenship: United Kingdom.

First publication of the text used: 1895 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from Russian in 1895 by Constance Garnett.' The colophon gives the original Russian publication as 1860.)

Why this is public domain:
- United States: works published before 1931 are in the public domain in the United States. The colophon dates this translation to 1895. The edition's rights statement (quoted below) says the same.
- Country of origin (original Russian text: Russia; translation: not stated by the colophon): Russia has a term of life plus 70 years. The last author of the original to die is Ivan Turgenev, in 1883, so the original is public domain in Russia from 1 January 1954. The Russian extension of 4 years for persons who worked or fought in World War II does not apply, because no person in the text is known to have done so. The translation's country is not stated. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life plus 70 years or less for these deaths. The last person to die among the people whose words are in the text is Constance Garnett, in 1946, so the translation is public domain in each of them by 1 January 2017.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: original publication 1860 by Ivan Turgenev; translated from Russian in 1895 by Constance Garnett
- Wikidata Q42831 (Ivan Turgenev), death year 1883
- Wikidata Q2495818 (Constance Garnett), death year 1946
